flawed_step: Step 4: a vertex cannot necessarily be inserted into a Hamiltonian cycle merely because it has one neighbor on that cycle; insertion requires two consecutive neighbors.
counterexample: Let P have vertices a_i,b_i for i modulo 5 and edges a_i a_{i+1}, a_i b_i, and b_i b_{i+2}. Then P is connected, P-v is Hamiltonian for every vertex v, but P is not Hamiltonian.
assessment_summary:
Proof attempt and full assessment:

1. Let G satisfy the hypotheses, fix v, and let C be a Hamiltonian cycle of G-v. — JUSTIFIED: such a cycle exists by hypothesis.

2. Every vertex of G other than v lies on C. — JUSTIFIED: this is the definition of a Hamiltonian cycle in G-v.

3. Since G is connected, v has a neighbor x, and x lies on C. — JUSTIFIED: a connected graph with at least four vertices has no isolated vertex, and Step 2 places every possible neighbor of v on C.

4. Insert v next to x in C to obtain a cycle through every vertex of G. — NOT JUSTIFIED: replacing an edge xy of C by x-v-y requires v to be adjacent to both consecutive vertices x and y. One neighbor on C is insufficient.

5. Therefore G has a Hamiltonian cycle. — NOT JUSTIFIED: this conclusion depends on the invalid insertion in Step 4.

The failure is substantive, as the following counterexample proves.

6. Define P with vertices a_i,b_i (i modulo 5) and edges a_i a_{i+1}, a_i b_i, and b_i b_{i+2}. — JUSTIFIED: this explicitly defines the Petersen graph as a finite simple graph on ten vertices.

7. P is connected. — JUSTIFIED: the a_i form a 5-cycle, and every b_i is joined to a_i by a spoke.

8. P is vertex-transitive. — JUSTIFIED: rotations i↦i+t are automorphisms, and the map a_i↦b_{2i}, b_i↦a_{2i} is also an automorphism; together these maps can send a_0 to any vertex.

9. P-a_0 has the Hamiltonian cycle a_1-a_2-a_3-a_4-b_4-b_2-b_0-b_3-b_1-a_1. — JUSTIFIED: all nine remaining vertices occur exactly once, and every consecutive pair is an edge from Step 6.

10. Consequently P-v is Hamiltonian for every vertex v. — JUSTIFIED: by Step 8 an automorphism sends v to a_0, and the inverse image of the cycle in Step 9 is a Hamiltonian cycle of P-v.

11. If P had a Hamiltonian cycle H, H would use either two or four spokes a_i b_i. — JUSTIFIED: the spokes are exactly the edges crossing between the sets {a_i} and {b_i}; a cycle crosses any cut an even number of times, must cross this cut at least once, and there are only five spokes.

12. H cannot use exactly two spokes. — JUSTIFIED: within each of the two induced 5-cycles, H would be a spanning path. If its spokes have indices p and q, the outer path requires q-p≡±1 mod 5, while the inner path requires q-p≡±2 mod 5, which is impossible.

13. H cannot use exactly four spokes. — JUSTIFIED: let the omitted spoke have index j and rotate so j=0. Degree two at every vertex forces the outer edges a_0a_1,a_0a_4,a_2a_3 and the inner edges b_0b_2,b_0b_3,b_1b_4. Together with the four spokes these form two disjoint 5-cycles, a_0-a_1-b_1-b_4-a_4-a_0 and a_2-a_3-b_3-b_0-b_2-a_2, rather than one Hamiltonian cycle.

14. Hence P is not Hamiltonian, although every P-v is Hamiltonian. — JUSTIFIED: Steps 11–13 exclude every possible Hamiltonian cycle, while Step 10 establishes the deletion property.

15. Therefore the proposed universal statement is false. — JUSTIFIED: P satisfies all stated definitions and the antecedent but not the conclusion.
